impact:
Found while verifying the 2026-08-31 deploy. ISS-047 added a durable per-tenant synthesis-status.json so a failure survives the process and can be surfaced. It is written server-side, but handleSyncPull does NOT include it in the pull payload — it returns observations, sessions, growth, reinforcements, lessons, persona, playbook and active, and nothing else.

CONSEQUENCE: for a synced user (ZUG_URL set, which is the paid/canonical path), ~/.zug/synthesis-status.json never appears. The T-058 dashboard reads that local file, so its "LAST SYNTHESIS" tile reads "never run" permanently, no matter what the server actually did. Confirmed on the live machine after deploy: the file is absent locally while the server has been running the new code.

The MCP zug_status tool is unaffected — it executes server-side and reads the server's copy — so the gap is specific to anything reading the local data directory. That is exactly the dashboard, and it will get worse as more views depend on locally-synced state.

Note the asymmetry this creates: the one surface built to make synthesis failure visible is the surface that cannot see it.

FIX DIRECTION: add `synthesisStatus` to PullResponse in sync-types.ts, return it from handleSyncPull, and write it in sync.ts's pull alongside persona/playbook/active. It is a single small JSON object with no merge semantics needed — last-writer-wins from the canonical server is correct, since the server is the only thing that synthesizes for a synced user.

Alternatively the dashboard could read status via the MCP tool rather than the file, but that turns a read-only local page into a network client, which the T-058 design deliberately avoided.
title: Synthesis status never reaches a synced client — dashboard always reports "never run"
